analysis: The code snippet calls errorListeners.toArray(new ErrorListener[errorListeners.size()]) where errorListeners is a Vector. The javadoc declares two exceptions: NullPointerException (if the array argument is null) and ArrayStoreException (if the runtime type of the array is not a supertype of every element). In this context, the array argument is newly created with new ErrorListener[...], so it is never null, thus NullPointerException condition is avoided. The array type is ErrorListener[], which is a supertype of the element type (presumably ErrorListener) because the Vector is parameterized with ErrorListener. Thus the runtime type compatibility is satisfied, avoiding ArrayStoreException. Therefore, both exceptions are fully avoided by the calling code.
answer: Both NullPointerException and ArrayStoreException are avoided.
remark: Both exceptions are avoided: NullPointerException because the passed array is non-null; ArrayStoreException because the array type matches the element type of the Vector.
